formation.title: The Principality of Moldavia
formation.text:
The banner of the aurochs flies over our principality. Moldavia stands at a crossroads: literally and figuratively. To the west, the Hungarian crown claims suzerainty. To the east, the Ottoman shadow grows longer with each passing year. To the north, Poland watches with interest.

Our voivode must choose how Moldavia will endure. Will we follow the path of Stephen the Great, building fortresses across every mountain pass and rallying the free peasantry into a citizen army? Or will we play the empires against each other, leveraging our position as a vital trade corridor to secure autonomy through diplomacy and prosperity?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We shall be the shield that never breaks

modifiers.name: Shield of Christendom
modifiers.text: The Principality of Moldavia stands as an Orthodox bastion, its fortresses and peasant armies guarding the eastern marches of Christian Europe against all who would threaten them.

options.text: We shall thrive between the great powers

modifiers.name: Crossroads Principality
modifiers.text: Moldavia thrives at the intersection of empires, turning its position between East and West into an advantage through shrewd diplomacy, cultural exchange, and lucrative transit trade.

advances.name: Plaiesi Tradition
advances.text: The plaiesi are free mountain peasants who guard the Carpathian passes, ambushing invaders and fighting delaying actions in terrain they know intimately.

advances.name: Boyar Privileges
advances.text: The great boyar families control vast landed estates, providing the principality with agricultural wealth and political counsel in the voivodal divan.

advances.name: Moldavian Apiculture
advances.text: Moldavia's forests teem with bees, and beeswax has become one of the principality's most valuable exports, traded as far as Constantinople and Venice.

advances.name: Orthodox Identity
advances.text: The Orthodox faith is inseparable from Moldavian identity, with the metropolitan see and monastic foundations serving as pillars of national consciousness.

advances.name: Razesi Mobilization
advances.text: The razesi (free landowning peasants) form the backbone of Moldavia's militia. Unlike serfs bound to noble estates, they fight for their own land and freedom.

advances.name: Calarasi Tactics
advances.text: The calarasi light cavalry employ Tatar-style hit-and-run tactics, harassing enemy columns, cutting supply lines, and drawing larger forces into ambushes.

advances.name: Fortress Builders
advances.text: Under the voivode's direction, a network of stone fortresses rises across Moldavia, from Suceava and Neamt in the west to Soroca and Tighina on the eastern frontier.

event.title: The Fortress Program
event.text:
Under the direction of the voivode, Moldavia has embarked on an unprecedented program of fortification. From the Carpathian passes to the Dniester marshes, a network of stone cetati now guards every approach to the heartland. The great fortress of Suceava, seat of the principality, has been reinforced with new walls and bastions. Cetatea Neamt crowns its mountain peak, commanding the Moldova valley. Soroca watches the eastern frontier, while Hotin guards the northern border.

This is not merely military construction: it is a declaration that Moldavia intends to endure. Shall we continue pouring resources into these defenses, or redirect our attention to training mobile field forces that can strike before the enemy reaches our walls?

options.text: Stone walls and deep ditches shall guard our land

modifiers.name: Cetatea Program
modifiers.text: A comprehensive fortress-building program modeled on the twenty-four strongholds constructed under the voivode's direction, each positioned to command a pass, ford, or crossroads.

options.text: Our cavalry shall be our fortress

modifiers.name: Open Field Doctrine
modifiers.text: Rather than shelter behind walls, Moldavia's cavalry sweeps the field, striking before the enemy can bring siege equipment to bear against our fortresses.

advances.name: Painted Churches
advances.text: The monasteries of northern Moldavia are adorned with vivid exterior frescoes: masterworks of Orthodox art that serve as open-air scriptures for the faithful.

event.title: The Painted Monasteries
event.text:
Something extraordinary is taking shape in the hills of northern Moldavia. The monasteries commissioned by our princes (Voronet, Moldovita, Humor, Sucevita) are being adorned not merely inside, but on their exterior walls with vivid frescoes depicting the Last Judgment, the Siege of Constantinople, and the lives of saints. These paintings, executed in brilliant blues and reds that seem to defy the passage of time, transform each monastery into an open Bible for the faithful.

The painted monasteries have become centers of learning, their scriptoriums producing chronicles and liturgical texts, their schools educating the sons of boyars and free peasants alike. They stand as proof that Moldavia is not merely a frontier marchland but a civilization in its own right.

options.text: Let our faith be painted upon the world

modifiers.name: Glory of Voronet
modifiers.text: The painted monasteries of Moldavia have become masterpieces of Orthodox art, their exterior frescoes inspiring pilgrims and scholars from across the Christian world.

advances.name: Suceava Court
advances.text: The princely court at Suceava, capital of Moldavia, serves as both a center of governance and a junction for trade routes connecting Central Europe to the Black Sea.

advances.name: Curteni Guard
advances.text: The curteni are the princely court cavalry: professional warriors maintained by the voivode as a standing force independent of the boyar military obligations.

advances.name: Voivodeship Arms
advances.text: The principality establishes its own armories, reducing dependence on imported weaponry and equipping the growing professional army with locally forged arms.

advances.name: Scorched Earth Doctrine
advances.text: Moldavia's defensive doctrine turns the principality's own terrain into a weapon: retreating forces destroy crops, poison wells, and fell trees to slow the invader.

event.title: The Doctrine of the Wilderness
event.text:
In January 1475, an Ottoman army of perhaps 120,000 men under Hadim Suleiman Pasha invaded Moldavia. Stephen the Great, commanding fewer than 40,000 troops, retreated before the advancing host, destroying crops and poisoning wells as he went. When the Ottomans reached the narrow valley at Vaslui, exhausted, hungry, and disoriented by fog, the Moldavian army fell upon them from the surrounding forests. The rout was total.

The Battle of Vaslui demonstrated that a small nation could defeat a vast empire, not through matching its strength, but through patience, terrain, and the willingness to destroy one's own land rather than surrender it. Pope Sixtus IV called Stephen 'Verus Christianae Fidei Athleta': the true champion of the Christian faith. Shall we codify this doctrine of defensive devastation, or perfect the ambush tactics that delivered the killing blow?

options.text: Let the land itself be our weapon

modifiers.name: Vaslui Doctrine
modifiers.text: The scorched earth strategy that devastated invading armies at Vaslui: destroying crops, poisoning wells, and turning the land itself into a weapon against the invader.

options.text: Perfect the art of the forest ambush

modifiers.name: Forest Ambush Mastery
modifiers.text: The art of the Moldavian forest ambush: luring superior forces into narrow valleys and dense woodland before falling upon them from every direction.

advances.name: Between Empires
advances.text:
Caught between Ottoman, Hungarian, and Polish ambitions, Moldavia has perfected the art of playing great powers against each other to preserve its autonomy, and forges its own arms rather than buy them from any of them.

Available in: Moldavian Armory

advances.name: Professional Army
advances.text: The lefegii are salaried professional soldiers who serve the voivode directly, providing a reliable core for the principality's army independent of feudal obligation.

advances.name: Moldavian Viticulture
advances.text:
The hill country of Moldavia produces renowned wines, with the boyar estates cultivating vineyards that supply both the domestic market and the export trade.

Available in: Boyar Estate

advances.name: Chronicle Tradition
advances.text: Moldavian monastic chroniclers record the history of the principality, preserving knowledge and fostering a tradition of literacy within the church.

advances.name: Tribute Diplomacy
advances.text: Moldavia pays tribute to maintain its internal autonomy: a pragmatic arrangement that preserves the principality's institutions while acknowledging overwhelming power.

advances.name: Iasi Ascendant
advances.text: As the princely seat shifts from Suceava to Iasi, the new capital becomes a center of learning and culture at the crossroads of east and west.

advances.name: Boyar Constitutionalism
advances.text: The great boyars assert constitutional limits on princely authority, establishing precedents for shared governance that restrain arbitrary rule.

advances.name: Printing Houses
advances.text: Orthodox printing houses in Moldavia produce liturgical texts, legal codes, and chronicles in the vernacular, spreading literacy beyond the monasteries.

advances.name: Enduring Resistance
advances.text: Despite centuries of foreign domination, Moldavian military traditions endure: the free peasantry still takes up arms when called, fighting with the desperation of those defending their own soil.

advances.name: Phanariot Reforms
advances.text: The Phanariot princes, though appointed by Constantinople, introduce Enlightenment-inspired administrative and legal reforms that modernize Moldavian governance.

advances.name: Emancipation
advances.text: The abolition of serfdom transforms Moldavian society, freeing the rural population to pursue opportunities beyond the boyar estates.

advances.name: National Awakening
advances.text: A growing consciousness of Moldavian and Romanian national identity spreads through the principality, fueled by literary movements and historical scholarship.

advances.name: Modern Army
advances.text: Moldavian military forces adopt modern European organization, drill, and equipment, transforming from feudal levies into a professional national army.

destiny.name: Destiny of Moldavia
destiny.text: The principality has been formed. Now its true destiny begins: whether as the shield of Christendom or the crossroads of empires.

event.title: The Destiny of Moldavia
event.text: Moldavia stands reborn. The aurochs banner flies over a united principality, and the question that has haunted every voivode since Bogdan the Founder can finally be answered not with hope, but with action. What shall Moldavia become? The principality's fate is no longer in the hands of foreign emperors and sultans. It rests with us alone.

options.text: Our destiny is our own to forge

destiny.name: Defender of the Passes
destiny.text: Secure the Wallachian heartland by taking Targoviste and Braila, uniting the Romanian lands under Moldavian military leadership. Requires an army of at least 30,000 men.

conditions.text: Moldavia follows the path of the Shield of Christendom
Own Târgoviște, or a subject owns it
Own Brăila, or a subject owns it

event.title: Defender of the Passes
event.text:
The Carpathian passes are secured, and our armies have crossed into Wallachia. Targoviste, seat of the Wallachian voivodes, flies the Moldavian banner. Braila, commanding the lower Danube, is ours. The Romanian lands begin to unite under the shield of Moldavian arms.

This is what Stephen the Great envisioned, not merely defending our borders, but extending them until no invader can threaten our heartland. The road south lies open. The Danube awaits.

options.text: The passes are ours. Now for the river.

destiny.name: Danube Bulwark
destiny.text: Extend Moldavian control along the Danube frontier. Take Constanta in Dobruja and Drastar on the Bulgarian bank, building a chain of fortifications that makes the river an impassable barrier.

conditions.text: Own Constanța, or a subject owns it
Own Drastar, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Danube Frontier
event.text:
Moldavian fortifications now line the Danube from Dobruja to the Bulgarian bank. Constanta gives us a window onto the Black Sea, while Drastar commands the river crossing that has seen armies pass for a thousand years. The ancient Roman limes, abandoned for centuries, lives again under the banner of the aurochs.

Our generals debate the next phase. Some advocate garrisoning these positions permanently, creating an unbreakable defensive line. Others argue for an aggressive frontier march: using the Danube as a springboard for further expansion rather than a static barrier.

options.text: Garrison the river. Let none cross.

modifiers.name: Danube Garrison
modifiers.text: Permanent garrisons along the Danube frontier maintain order, recover from devastation rapidly, and build a tradition of professional military service.

options.text: The frontier is a springboard, not a wall.

modifiers.name: Border March
modifiers.text: An aggressive frontier doctrine that uses the Danube as a springboard for raids and expansion, though the constant warfare takes its toll on local production.

destiny.name: Champion of the Faith
destiny.text: The ultimate expression of the Shield of Christendom: plant the banner of the aurochs over Constantinople and Varna, fulfilling the crusading vision that Stephen the Great only dreamed of.

conditions.text: Own Constantinople, or a subject owns it
Own Varna, or a subject owns it

event.title: Champion of the Faith
event.text:
The unthinkable has been achieved. Constantinople, the Queen of Cities, the seat of emperors and patriarchs, flies the banner of the aurochs. Varna, where a crusade once perished, is redeemed. Pope Sixtus called Stephen 'Verus Christianae Fidei Athleta': the true champion of the Christian faith. We have earned that title a hundredfold.

Moldavia's transformation from a frontier principality to a great Christian power is complete. But greatness demands choices. Shall we wield this power as Orthodox crusaders, extending the true faith across the lands we have conquered? Or shall we build an eternal bulwark, an impregnable fortress-state that no power on earth can overthrow?

options.text: We are the sword of the Orthodox faith

modifiers.name: Orthodox Champion
modifiers.text: Moldavia wields its newfound power as a sword of the Orthodox faith, commanding respect in peace negotiations while keeping conquered peoples loyal through shared religion.

options.text: We are the wall that shall never fall

modifiers.name: Eternal Bulwark
modifiers.text: A fortress-state doctrine that reduces military costs and improves tactical doctrine, though the focus on fortification diverts resources from civilian construction.

destiny.name: Gateway Between Worlds
destiny.text: Establish Moldavia as the essential trade corridor between East and West by securing Lviv, the great western trading hub, and accumulating substantial treasury reserves.

conditions.text: Moldavia follows the path of the Crossroads Principality
Own Lviv, or a subject owns it

event.title: Gateway Between Worlds
event.text:
Lviv has entered Moldavia's commercial orbit, and with it the trade routes that connect the Baltic to the Black Sea, Central Europe to the Orient. Moldavian merchants now handle goods that once passed through foreign hands: Flemish cloth moving east, Crimean furs moving west, spices from the Levant passing through our warehouses.

The voivode's treasury swells with customs revenue. What empires could not take by force, Moldavia gains through the shrewdness of its merchants and the advantage of its geography.

options.text: Let the wealth of nations flow through our lands

destiny.name: Emporium of the East
destiny.text: Transform Moldavia into a major economic power. Ensure wine flows through the capital market, build beeswax houses in two places to render the wax our carts take up the road to Lviv, and build up Cetatea Alba, the port at the mouth of the Dniester where the road from Lviv meets the Black Sea.

children.text: Wine is produced in the market
Wine is traded in the market

conditions.text: At least 2 of our locations have a Beeswax House
We own Cetatea Alba and its development is at least 16

event.title: Emporium of the East
event.text:
Moldavian wine is traded in markets from Venice to Constantinople. The wax of a hundred forest villages is rendered in Moldavian houses and carted up the road to Lviv, and from there to Danzig and Venice. At Cetatea Alba, below the walls the princes raised, ships load what the carts from Lviv bring down to the sea. What was once a frontier marchland is now a prosperous commercial state.

Our advisors present two visions for the next stage. Some advocate deepening our commercial infrastructure: more markets, more warehouses, more trade agreements. Others argue that our true strength lies in cultural exchange: becoming a bridge between Latin West and Orthodox East, drawing scholars, artists, and diplomats to our courts.

options.text: Commerce is the sinew of the state

modifiers.name: Trade Emporium
modifiers.text: Moldavia's commercial infrastructure expands, attracting more merchants and reducing borrowing costs, though rapid growth brings inflationary pressure.

options.text: We shall be the bridge between civilizations

modifiers.name: Cultural Bridge
modifiers.text: Moldavia becomes a diplomatic hub between civilizations, expanding its influence through relationships and vassal loyalty, though its pacifist reputation makes wars more costly to justify.

destiny.name: Dacia Reborn
destiny.text: Unite the Romanian lands through culture and prosperity rather than conquest alone. Take Bucharest, and Brasov beyond the mountains, where the first books in Romanian were printed, and become a beacon of prestige and wealth.

conditions.text: Own Bucharest, or a subject owns it
Own Brașov, or a subject owns it

event.title: Dacia Reborn
event.text:
The dream of a united Romania, not through blood and iron alone, but through shared language, culture, and prosperity, is taking shape. Bucharest, jewel of the Wallachian plain, recognizes Moldavian leadership. Brasov, where the first books in Romanian came off the press, sends them from the Carpathians to the Danube. Scholars speak of Dacia reborn: the ancient kingdom rising from the ashes of a thousand years.

Moldavia stands at a crossroads once more, but this time as a power rather than a pawn. Shall we forge a new Dacian identity, assimilating the diverse peoples of our realm into a unified nation? Or shall we pursue an enlightenment vision: tolerant, cosmopolitan, drawing strength from diversity rather than uniformity?

options.text: One people, one language, one destiny

modifiers.name: Dacia Nova
modifiers.text: The new Dacian state unifies its peoples through shared identity, satisfying all estates while assimilating diverse populations and expanding diplomatic reach.

modifiers.name: Moldavian Enlightenment
modifiers.text: An enlightenment vision that spreads letters and integrates diverse peoples through tolerance, though the nobility's military obligations diminish as cultural pursuits take precedence.

units.name: Plaiesi
units.text: Mountain border guards drawn from the free peasantry of the Carpathian passes. The plaiesi know every trail and defile, fighting as skirmishers who ambush invaders and melt back into the forests.

units.name: Razesi Militia
units.text: Free landowning peasants mobilized for the defense of Moldavia. Unlike serfs, the razesi fight for their own land, making them stubborn and determined defenders.

units.name: Calarasi
units.text: Moldavian light cavalry who employ Tatar-style hit-and-run tactics. The calarasi harass enemy columns, raid supply lines, and draw superior forces into ambush positions.

units.name: Curteni Guard
units.text: The court cavalry of the Moldavian voivode: professional horsemen maintained as a standing force independent of boyar feudal obligations. They form the shock arm of the principality's army.

units.name: Lefegii
units.text: Salaried professional infantry in the service of the voivode. The lefegii provide a disciplined core for the Moldavian army, trained in close-order formation fighting.

buildings.name: Cetate
buildings.text: A Moldavian mountain fortress built to command a pass, ford, or crossroads. These stone strongholds form a defensive network across the principality.

buildings.name: Painted Monastery
buildings.text: A Moldavian monastery adorned with vivid exterior frescoes, serving as a center of Orthodox learning, art, and spiritual life.

buildings.name: Boyar Estate
buildings.text: The landed estate of a Moldavian boyar, producing agricultural wealth from vineyards, livestock, and forestry.

where.text: Wine is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Moldavian Armory
buildings.text: A workshop producing weapons and equipment for the principality's growing military forces.

buildings.name: Beeswax House
buildings.text: The wax house of the forest beekeepers. The combs of the hives are pressed, boiled and cast into cakes of yellow wax, and more of the land's wax reaches the carts that take it up the road to Lviv. It can stand only where the land yields beeswax.

where.text: The location's raw material is Beeswax

buildings.name: Moldavian Printing House
buildings.text: An Orthodox printing house producing liturgical texts, chronicles, and legal codes in the Moldavian vernacular.

buildings.name: Moldavian Citadel
buildings.text: A grand fortress representing the apex of Moldavian defensive architecture: massive stone walls, deep ditches, and permanent garrison quarters that make this location virtually impregnable.

buildings.name: Moldavian Academy
buildings.text: A center of Romanian learning and culture, where scholars, theologians, and artists gather to study, teach, and advance the intellectual life of the nation.

list.name: Sfatul Domnesc
list.text: The Princely Council of great boyars that advised the hospodar and elected new princes from candidates of the ruling house. The council comprised the Mare Vornic (chief justice), Mare Logofat (chancellor), Mare Vistier (treasurer), Mare Spatar (sword-bearer and military commander), and Mare Postelnic, drawn from the great families whose genealogies link the fifteenth-century rolls to Stephen the Great's reign of 1457-1504. By binding ducal decisions to consultative assent, the Sfatul anchored Moldavian constitutional life until the Phanariot interlude after 1711.

list.name: Mitropolia of Suceava
list.text: The autonomous Moldavian Orthodox see established at Suceava in 1386 and recognised in 1401 by the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople under metropolitan Joseph, with three suffragan bishoprics covering the entire principality. The Mitropolia anointed the hospodar, and a prince without its sanction was one claimant among many. It supplied literate clerks to the chancery from the Putna and Neamt monastery scriptoria, and translated patriarchal canons for use in Moldavian courts. The seat moved permanently from Suceava to Iasi in 1677, but the institution's continuity across three centuries gave the church a constitutional weight second only to the Sfatul Domnesc.

list.name: Razesi Free Villages
list.text: The landed free peasantry of Moldavia, organised as obste village communities led by a cneaz and holding land in joint ownership across an open-field system. Stephen the Great drew the oastea cea mica from these freeholders, raising voinici infantry and hansari light cavalry directly from the razesi rolls in exchange for fiscal privileges and pasture rights. The free villages reduced the prince's dependence on boyar retinues and supplied the social base that made Moldavian armies disproportionately mobile through the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.

list.name: Pravila of Vasile Lupu
list.text: The Carte romaneasca de invatatura promulgated at Iasi in 1646, the first printed legal code in Moldavia and the first official codification of civil law composed in Romanian using Cyrillic script. Compiled under Vasile Lupu (1634-1653) by the logothete Eustratie, the Pravila drew on the Leges Coloniariae of Justinian II, Leunclavius's Jus Graeco-Romanum (Frankfurt 1596), and Farinacci's Praxis et theoricae criminalis (Venice 1610), supplementing them with Moldavian customary norms on land, debt, and crime. Issued from the Trei Ierarhi monastery press, the code bound the hospodar's courts to written procedure.

list.name: Vornicii of Tara de Sus and Tara de Jos
list.text: The dual provincial governorships dividing medieval Moldavia into the Upper Country centred on Suceava and the Lower Country administered from the Bârlad-Iasi axis. Each Mare Vornic exercised judicial appellate jurisdiction over his half of the principality, supervised the parcalabi of the fortress districts and the parcalabia clerks, collected the prince's share of fines and confiscations, and led the regional levy in war. The division survived the Phanariot reorganisation as a residual fiscal-judicial framework and gave the great boyar dynasties of each half a regional power base outside the capital court.

list.name: Phanariot Administration
list.text: The post-1711 governing apparatus installed when the Porte began appointing Greek hospodars from the Phanar district of Constantinople, beginning with Nicholas Mavrocordatos in Moldavia and continuing until the 1821 Greek revolt. Phanariot voivodes copied Petrine and Habsburg models: they made noble rank dependent on state service, regularised the capitation, and under Constantine Mavrocordatos abolished the legal serfdom of the rumâni in Moldavia in 1749. Greek became the language of court business, the Iasi Princely Academy was reorganised as the Domneasca, and tribute-extracting fiscalism kept tenures short and administrations indebted to the Constantinople bankers.
